description: The ego-self; the primal sense of 'I-ness' (hau = I, mai = I-am) that keeps the soul separate from the Divine — Gurbani's central obstacle on the spiritual path, overcome only by Guru's grace.
caveats: ਹਉ (750 hits) is the ordinary first-person pronoun 'I/me' and is excluded; though philosophically the pronoun itself encodes ego, it is far too grammatically pervasive to index as a doctrinal concept word.

description: The mind — the restless inner faculty that oscillates between attachment and liberation; Gurbani's most frequent single concept-word, serving as both the obstacle (manmukh mind) and the instrument of devotion (man tanu dhan).
caveats: ਮਨਾਂ (1) and ਮਨੀ (3) are negligible and excluded. ਮਨੋ may occasionally be a postposition ('from the mind') rather than the noun itself but is included as inseparable from the mind-concept.

description: The illusory world of material attachment; the three-guned phenomenal creation that enchants the soul away from the True One — used consistently as the great veil of spiritual forgetfulness.
caveats: ਮਾਇ (74 hits) is primarily 'mother' (ਮਾਇ ਬਾਪ = mother and father) and is excluded. While ਮਾਇ can carry the maya-sense in some compound constructions, the majority usage is parental and would inflate the count deceptively.

description: Worldly attachment and emotional entanglement — the sticky love for family, possessions, and transient things that binds the soul; closely paired with maya in compound phrases like ਮਾਇਆ ਮੋਹ.
caveats: ਮੋਹਨ (30 hits) is a divine epithet ('the Enchanter', a name of God/Krishna) and is excluded from this concept; lines like 'ਮੋਹਨ ਲਾਲ' clearly refer to Waheguru, not attachment.

description: Lust and sensual desire — the first of the five thieves (panj chor); ਕਾਮਣਿ (woman/beloved) is included as it frequently appears in the context of lustful distraction from the Divine.
caveats: ਕਾਮਣਿ also figures in bridal-mysticism imagery (the soul as bride longing for God), making its valence dual. Included because even in bride-imagery the word sits in the kaam semantic field. ਕਾਮੀ includes 'ਨਿਹਕਾਮੀ' (desireless) — query results should filter compound forms for precise analysis.

description: Anger and wrath — the second of the five vices; its poison destroys inner peace and burns the body-vessel, contrasted with the cool fragrance of Nam.
caveats: Variant spellings ਕੋਧ/ਕੋਧੁ checked — zero hits; all Gurbani usage is the full ਕ੍ਰੋਧ form. ਕ੍ਰੋਧਾ/ਕ੍ਰੋਧੈ also zero.

description: Greed and covetousness — the third vice; the insatiable hunger for wealth and more, which drives the manmukh to endless worldly striving.
caveats: ਲੋਭੈ = 0 hits. All five confirmed forms accounted for.

description: Egotistical pride and arrogance — the fifth vice; the puffed-up sense of personal greatness. ਅਭਿਮਾਨ (Sanskrit abhimāna) is used as a near-synonym alongside ਅਹੰਕਾਰ throughout the Bani.
caveats: ਅਹੰਕਾਰੈ and ਅਭਿਮਾਨੀਆ = 0 hits. Note: haumai and ahankar overlap conceptually but are distinct words — haumai is the subtler ego-sense while ahankar/abhiman is the outward arrogant display.

description: The paired poles of suffering (dukh) and ease/peace (sukh) — Gurbani presents them as two faces of the same maya-conditioned existence; true liberation lies beyond both in the equipoise of sahaj.
caveats: ਦੁਖੈ = 0 hits. This is the largest combined concept by hit-count; queries should filter by the dukh- and sukh- sub-clusters separately when needed.

description: Doubt, delusion, and wandering — the state of spiritual confusion where the soul mistakes illusion for reality; both ਭਰਮ (Punjabi form) and ਭ੍ਰਮ (Sanskrit-closer form) are used throughout the SGGS.
caveats: ਭਰਮੀ and ਭ੍ਰਮੀ = 0 hits. The two spelling families (ਭਰਮ-/ਭ੍ਰਮ-) are phonological variants of the same word and should be treated as one concept.

description: Craving and insatiable thirst — the restless desire that can never be quenched by worldly objects; closely related to lobh but emphasises the burning thirst-quality of unfulfilled longing.
caveats: ਤ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨਾ (with explicit ਸ਼) = 0 hits — the corpus uses ਸ not ਸ਼. ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ/ਤਿਖਾ mean 'thirst/burning thirst' and are included as direct semantic synonyms.

description: Intuitive poise, natural ease, and equipoise of the realised state — the effortless, spontaneous condition of the soul absorbed in the Divine; the antithesis of the five vices' turbulence.
caveats: ਸਹਜੋ/ਸਹਜੋਊ = 0/1 hit respectively; ਸਹਜੋਊ is a single outlier and excluded. Minor compound forms like ਸਹਜਾਇਆ (2), ਸਹਜਾਏ (2), ਸਹਜਾਰੀ (1) are derived verbs/adjectives and excluded from the core noun-concept index.

description: Divine bliss — the supreme joy that pervades the soul in union with Waheguru; the subject of Guru Amar Das's celebrated Anand Sahib and a frequent marker of the gurmukh state.
caveats: Both ਅ- and ਆ- prefix spellings are phonological variants of the same Sanskrit ānanda; treated as one concept. ਅਨੰਦੈ and ਆਨੰਦੈ = 0 hits.

description: Contentment — the virtue of being satisfied with the Divine will (hukam); one of the five virtues (panj gun) and the antidote to lobh/trishna; paired with sat, daya, dharam, and dhairy in classical Gurbani virtue-lists.
caveats: ਸੰਤੋਸ਼/ਸੰਤੋਸ = 0 hits — the corpus uses only the ਖ form, not the ਸ਼ variant.

description: Compassion — both as a divine attribute (God as Dayal, the Compassionate) and as a human virtue to be cultivated; the fifth of the panj gun alongside sat, santokh, dharam, and dhairy.
caveats: The majority of hits are for God described as Dayal (compassionate/merciful), not humans practising compassion — queries should disambiguate theological uses from ethical injunctions. ਦਇਆਲੂ/ਦਇਆਵਾਨ = 0 hits.

description: Selfless service — devotional service to the Guru and Sangat as the primary praxis of bhakti; the gurmukh who serves without ego earns liberation while the manmukh serves only self-interest.
caveats: All forms are clearly within the seva semantic field. ਸੇਵ (136) includes verbal/imperative uses ('serve!') alongside the noun.

description: Holy company — the congregation of truth-seekers (sangat), the company of the saints (sadhsangat/satsangat/satsangi); one of the most powerful liberating forces in Gurbani alongside Nam and Guru.
caveats: ਸੰਗ (40 hits) is a general preposition/noun meaning 'with/company' — only a subset refers to holy company specifically. Included for completeness but line-level analysis should filter. ਸੰਗਤ (without ਿ) = 0 hits.

description: The Guru-facing one — the soul oriented toward the Guru/Divine, the ideal spiritual being in Gurbani; contrasted with manmukh at every turn as the one who transcends the five vices through Guru's grace.
caveats: ਗੁਰਮੁਖੁ = 0 hits (the nominative ਿ form dominates overwhelmingly). The instrumental/locative ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ is the working form in almost all lines.

description: The self-willed, mind-facing one — the soul enslaved to its own ego and the five vices, living in maya's delusion; the negative archetype that epitomises the un-awakened human condition.
caveats: All four grammatical forms confirmed. The distribution across ਮਨਮੁਖ (direct), ਮਨਮੁਖਿ (oblique), and ਮਨਮੁਖੁ (nominative) is nearly even, indicating use across many grammatical roles.

description: Humility — expressed through multiple Punjabi/Braj words meaning lowly, poor in spirit, without pride; Gurbani elevates these as the ideal self-perception before the Divine, the opposite of ahankar.
caveats: ਨਿਮ੍ਰਤਾ (the Sanskrit loanword) = 0 hits; Gurbani uses indigenous vocabulary instead. ਦੀਨ/ਦੀਨੁ is polysemous: it means (1) humble/supplicant — the prevalent Gurbani usage in phrases like 'deen dayaal'; and (2) the Arabic dīn (faith/religion), e.g. in Bhai Gurdas and Bhagat Kabir lines. Both senses are present; contextual filtering is needed. ਨੀਚ/ਨੀਚੁ positively connotes self-abnegation before God (Nanak calls himself neechu) but can also mean literally low-caste — context determines valence. ਹਲੀਮੀ = 0 hits.
